prompts.units: Use case: historical-scene. Production game sprite atlas for Hundred Years War France and England 1337–1453. EXACT 4 columns x 4 rows equal cells on square 2048 canvas, 16 separate miniatures, isolated on actual transparent background. No borders, no labels, no text. Detailed painterly realistic historical strategy miniatures, earthy cloth, aged steel, subtle gold, consistent isometric three-quarter view facing lower right, generous empty margins in EVERY cell, full objects never cross cell boundaries. Order left-to-right top-to-bottom: row1 linen peasant with axe; French spear infantry in padded jack and kettle hat; English longbowman with tall yew longbow and quiver wearing muted red; English mounted bowman with long yew bow on plain horse (western medieval NOT Mongol). Row2 English knight on horse red caparison mail and transitional plate bascinet; French knight on horse blue caparison small gold fleurs de lis transitional plate; French crossbowman with crossbow and pavise; French ordonnance cavalry circa1445 on horse with lance and plate armor. Row3 French franc archer circa1448 with bow and padded jack; Genoese crossbowman carrying large pavise; Scottish foot spearman mail and blue tunic (no tartan kilt); routier mercenary with spear and worn brigandine. Row4 clinker-built northern cog ship with SINGLE square sail and high wooden castles; Mediterranean galley with lateen sail and banks of oars; short thick wrought iron bombard barrel on low heavy wooden cradle no modern carriage; French royal cannon circa1450 long iron barrel on timber wheeled bed. Period correct 14th and early15th century. No fantasy, horns, muskets, modern flags, crusader Templar costumes, eastern armor. Readable silhouettes at small size.
prompts.buildings: Use case: historical-scene. Production transparent RTS architecture and terrain sprite atlas for France and England Hundred Years War 1337–1453. EXACT 4 columns x 3 rows equal square cells, landscape 1536x1152. 12 separate complete objects centered with generous transparent padding, no overlaps, no labels, no gridlines, actual transparent background. Beautiful hand-painted isometric historical game miniatures, limestone, oak timber frames, slate and thatch, muted warm natural colors and consistent upper-left daylight. Order row1: French royal fortified Gothic palace with blue pennant (medieval Louvre inspired not Renaissance); English royal stone keep and curtain walls red pennant; French walled town compact half timber houses Gothic church; English village thatched cottages and timber barn. Row2: medieval timber and stone military courtyard barracks with weapon racks; cultivated wheat strip fields with fence tiny barn; French round-towered stone fortress and gatehouse blue pennant; medieval wooden river harbor wharf warehouse crane. Row3: compact French half timber village cottages; grey rocky European mountain outcrop sparse grass; clustered broadleaf oaks and beech trees; medieval iron mine rocky entrance wooden supports ore cart. Small natural footprints, no giant ground tiles, no modern features, no fantasy architecture, no onion domes, no Asian pagodas, no star forts, no writing.
prompts.heroes: Use case: historical-scene. Production character sprite atlas for Hundred Years War game. EXACT 5 columns x 5 rows of equal square cells on square canvas 2048. EXACTLY 25 individual full-body historical commander miniatures, standing on foot facing slightly lower right, consistent scale and style, each entirely inside own cell with generous transparent padding, actual transparent background no text no labels no borders. Elegant realistic hand-painted strategy illustration, expressive visible individual faces, authentic mail, bascinets and transitional plate for 14th century and simple French/English plate harness for 15th, natural fabrics no fantasy or giant pauldrons. Restrained red English accents for first12, blue French accents last13. Each commander distinguished by face age armor and heraldic cloth, bareheaded or open visor. Row1: Edward III mature bearded king in 1340s mail and plate red royal surcoat small crown; Edward Black Prince young dark haired in darkened steel and red heraldic jupon NOT fantasy black; Henry of Grosmont bearded veteran red cloak; John Chandos older one-eyed knight white surcoat red accent; Robert Knolles rugged mercenary with longbow leather jack. Row2: John of Gaunt tall noble red and gold; Henry Percy Hotspur young red haired knight; Henry V clean shaven young king early 15th plate red royal tabard; John Bedford middle aged dark hair blue-red quartered tabard; Thomas Montagu Salisbury mature bearded commander with sword. Row3: John Talbot elderly stern grey-haired veteran red surcoat; John Fastolf older knight holding longbow; Philip VI crowned bearded king 1340 mail transitional plate blue fleur de lis surcoat; Joan of Arc young 19-year-old woman SHORT dark cropped hair modest plain practical 1429 plate harness no makeup no sexualization holding tall white religious banner with subtle small gold motifs full banner contained inside cell; John II middle-aged bearded king blue royal surcoat mail and plate. Row4: Bertrand du Guesclin stocky rugged broad-faced knight simple worn steel white surcoat black eagle motif; Olivier de Clisson one-eyed mature knight red-white cloth; Jean de Vienne naval commander in blue cloth mail with sword; Boucicaut lean refined knight early15th steel and blue; John Stewart Earl of Buchan Scottish noble with long spear and blue cloth no kilt. Row5: La Hire red-haired fierce veteran in plate red-blue accent; Jean de Dunois young dark haired commander blue-gold tabard; Arthur de Richemont mature Breton commander blue-white surcoat; Poton de Xaintrailles rugged brown haired knight blue sash; Jean Bureau middle-aged artillery master plain wool cap and blue-brown coat holding measuring rod and small scroll. No horses, no backgrounds, no modern flags, no Renaissance outfits.
prompts.title: Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: full bleed landscape 1536x1024 key art background for a historical strategy game's title menu. Hundred Years War France and England, 1337–1453. Atmospheric painterly museum-quality oil and gouache illustration, sophisticated muted colors, graphite navy shadows, warm parchment light, restrained aged gold, crimson and ultramarine accents. View over northern French river landscape and a distant stone walled Gothic town at dawn, layers of mist, fortified bridge, distant rolling farmland. LEFT foreground English knight in historically plausible circa1400 mail and transitional steel plate bascinet with red cloth and lance, RIGHT foreground French knight in early15th steel and blue cloth with small gold fleur de lis and tall banner. Both viewed from behind or side looking into valley, horses if desired, no combat. Leave central upper half quiet misty dark blue for UI text and lower center dark for menu. Rich evocative illustrated chronicle, historical restraint. No writing, no watermark, no modern flags, no fantasy castles, no dragons, no horned helmets, no firearms.
